history.heading: Dutch colony
paragraphs: Suriname, on the northeast coast of South America, was home to indigenous peoples such as the Arawak and Carib. The English founded a colony in 1650, but the Dutch took it in 1667 in exchange for New Amsterdam (New York). Plantations of sugar, coffee and cotton used enslaved Africans, many of whom escaped into the rainforest and formed Maroon communities that fought for and won autonomy.
Slavery was abolished in 1863, followed by a ten-year transition. Indentured labourers then came from India, Java (Indonesia) and China, creating one of the world's most diverse societies.

history.heading: Independence
paragraphs: Suriname became independent on 25 November 1975, and many Surinamese moved to the Netherlands. Dési Bouterse led a military coup in 1980; in December 1982, 15 opponents were executed. A civil war with Maroon rebels followed in 1986–92. Bouterse was later elected president (2010–2020) and convicted for the 1982 murders. In 2025 Jennifer Geerlings-Simons became Suriname's first female president.

culture.heading: A mosaic of cultures
paragraphs: Dutch is the official language, and Sranan Tongo is the common language, along with Sarnami Hindustani, Javanese, Maroon languages and others. The population includes Hindustani (Indian), Creole, Maroon, Javanese, indigenous, Chinese and mixed communities. Hinduism, Christianity and Islam are practised, and a mosque and synagogue stand side by side in Paramaribo, whose historic centre is a UNESCO site.
Roti, pom (a baked dish) and nasi goreng reflect the diverse heritage. About 90 percent of Suriname is covered by rainforest.

politics.heading: Republic
paragraphs: Suriname is a republic in which the National Assembly elects the president, who is head of state and government. Parties are often organised along ethnic lines.

economy.heading: Resources
paragraphs: Gold, oil and formerly bauxite are the main exports. A major offshore oil discovery is expected to begin production around 2028. Rice, bananas and timber are also produced. Suriname faced a debt crisis and high inflation in the early 2020s. The currency is the Surinamese dollar.
